steps.title: Welcome!
steps.text: The guitar has 6 strings, a neck with frets, and a body that amplifies the sound. Strings are numbered from the thinnest (1st, high E) to the thickest (6th, low E).

steps.prompt: How many strings does a standard guitar have?

steps.title: Seated posture
steps.text: Sit up straight, rest the guitar on your right leg (right-handed). The neck points slightly upward. Your left-hand thumb goes behind the neck.

steps.title: Right hand
steps.text: The thumb (p), index (i), middle (m), and ring (a) fingers play the strings. Start by plucking an open string with the thumb, top to bottom.

steps.prompt: Where does the left-hand thumb go?

steps.title: Tuning EADGBE
steps.text: From thickest to thinnest string: E - A - D - G - B - E. Mnemonic: 'My Friend Gives Great Extra Blessings'.
Tune the 6th string (low E). Pluck the string and adjust the tuning peg until the tuner turns green.

steps.prompt: How many strings did you tune in this lesson?
How many strings did you tune in this lesson?

steps.text: Tune the 1st string (high E).

steps.title: Playing open strings
steps.text: Play the 1st string (the thinnest) with your right-hand index finger. It should sound clear and sustained. If it buzzes, press closer to the fret.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: This is how the open 1st string (E) should sound.

steps.prompt: If a string sounds muted or buzzes, what do you do?

steps.title: Frets
steps.text: Each fret raises a semitone. On the 1st string: fret 0 = E, 1 = F, 2 = F#, 3 = G.

steps.prompt: How many semitones does one fret raise?
